articles.title: Social isolation harms the aging brain independently of loneliness
articles.summary: New research reveals that physical social isolation harms the aging brain independently of subjective feelings of loneliness. Simulated public health interventions show that reconnecting isolated older adults can directly protect against cognitive decline.

articles.title: Who do teens crush on? A new study reveals the social math of adolescent attraction
articles.summary: A study of nearly 2,000 Dutch high schoolers reveals that when it comes to being someone's crush, a strong network of friends and one-on-one interactions matter far more than a widespread reputation for physical attractiveness.

articles.title: Psychopathic individuals more tolerant of online dating deception, study finds
articles.summary: A new study reveals that people with psychopathic traits are much more likely to excuse blatant deceptions on dating apps, such as lying about relationship status, age, or even gender.

articles.title: Introverts experience greater mood elevations from antidepressant placebos than extraverts
articles.summary: A new study indicates that introverts and individuals with lower natural joy experience the greatest mood boosts from dopamine-altering drugs and antidepressant placebos. The findings suggest that baseline personality heavily influences how people respond to mood treatments.

articles.title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their “stress hormone” already elevated
articles.summary: Frequent cannabis users may wake up with unusually high levels of the stress hormone cortisol, suggesting their daily stress rhythms could be disrupted. Researchers say the finding raises questions about whether using cannabis for stress relief might, over time, interfere with the very system that helps the body handle stress.

articles.title: Scientists say just 7 days of meditation can rewire your brain
articles.summary: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief. Participants also showed brain connectivity patterns resembling those associated with psychedelic experiences, suggesting that powerful altered states may be achievable without drugs.

articles.title: Stress can scramble your brain’s internal GPS, MRI study finds
articles.summary: Stress may literally scramble the brain’s internal GPS. Researchers found that cortisol, a hormone released during stress, made people significantly worse at navigating a virtual environment and disrupted the precise activity of grid cells, specialized brain cells that help us understand where we are in space. When landmarks were missing, this navigation system nearly stopped functioning, while another brain region appeared to step in and compensate.

articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary: Teens who start using cannabis may experience slower growth in memory, attention, language, and processing speed. Their abilities often developed normally at first, then began leveling off while nonusers continued improving. THC appeared to be the most likely driver, especially for worsening memory.

articles.title: Towards an Argumentative Foundation for Evaluative AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluative AI (EAI) has been recently proposed as a way to support human decision-making, not by producing a single recommendation, but by presenting competing hypotheses together with evidence for and against each. In this position paper, we advocate (computational) argumentation as a particularly suitable paradigm to provide a formal, computable foundation for forms of EAI that are explainable and contestable, setting the ground for a long-term research agenda towards distributed and human-centred EAI systems.

articles.title: Flow-by-Flow:Content-Judgment Bypass for Governing AI Output in High-Loss Domains
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prior work showed that human-in-the-loop oversight becomes structurally untenable in high-loss domains when AI output velocity V exceeds human cognitive capacity C_max. The operative constraint, however, is not V alone but V x L, where L denotes per-item cognitive load. L consists of triage, judgment, and response, which respond asymmetrically to AI capability improvement. Triage cost does not decline as models become more capable, because semantic indeterminacy is inherent in general-purpose design. Response cost is invariant to accuracy improve

articles.title: Data-Driven Fire-Zone Segmentation for Improved Short-Term Wildfire Prediction
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wildfire prediction models typically discretize study areas into uniform grids, ignoring the heterogeneous spatial distribution of ignitions. articles.title: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) integrate heterogeneous modalities through modality alignment and fusion, enabling stronger understanding and reasoning. However, this architectural shift reshapes the safety landscape of machine learning. articles.title: Tracing sources of epistemic uncertainty in deep learning predictions: homo- and hetero-scedastic linearized estimators
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We adapt two classical statistical estimators for quantifying uncertainty to modern deep learning, in order to provide clearer insights into uncertainty attributable to two sources : aleatoric uncertainty, or locally scarce data. Our approach leverages recent advances in approximate Fisher Information Matrices, to enable scaling to actual architectures.
